svg.title: How people reach the Lab
svg.desc: Three numbered access patterns lead into one Lab, the web app and API in an internal Azure Container Apps environment with public network access off. The Terraform default allows traffic from the management subnet, but Azure Bastion and the jumpbox are optional resources that are off by default. Path 1 shows a presenter or admin, while customers watch a shared screen, connecting over HTTPS to optional Azure Bastion, then by remote desktop to an optional jumpbox with a private IP address, which reaches the Lab across virtual network peering. Path 2, a design reference that is not deployed: an internal employee on an approved private network, such as VPN or ExpressRoute, connects over HTTPS to an Azure Application Gateway WAF v2 with a private frontend in a dedicated gateway subnet, which reaches the Lab over virtual network routing and private DNS. A public listener on the same gateway would serve regional internet users instead. Path 3, an optional draft that is off by default: a customer on the public internet connects to a public Azure Front Door Premium endpoint, where a web application firewall blocks clients that are not allowed. Front Door reaches the Lab through a Front Door-managed Private Link connection to the Container Apps environment, which an operator approves, and sends origin HTTPS requests. Private Link protects the Front Door to Lab hop, not the user to Front Door hop. The Lab has an ingress allow list. Rule 1 admits the management subnet by default; it doesn't provision an access machine. Rule 2 admits a gateway subnet and is not added yet. Rule 3 admits the traffic that arrives over the Front Door Private Link connection and is added only when Front Door is on. Anything not listed gets a 403. The Lab then calls Foundry, Cosmos DB and Storage privately with a managed identity. A caveat says the Lab has no end-user sign-in yet, so before customers use it themselves it needs Microsoft Entra ID sign-in and per-user ownership of saved records. A WAF, Private Link or managed identity does not provide those checks. This is a logical view, not a resource inventory.
svg.text: The management-subnet allow rule is default; Bastion and the jumpbox are optional and off by default.
The default rule allows this subnet, but it doesn't create an access machine or route.
Chat is capped at 20 turns a minute: enough for one presenter, tight for a group.
Needs a gateway subnet, an ingress rule for it, and private DNS to the Lab's address.
A public listener would serve regional internet users instead. Sign-in comes first.
Draft today: the WAF admits only listed single IPs. Private Link guards Front Door to the Lab only.
Opening it to customers needs sign-in, a custom domain, and each public resource approved.
